items.title: Microsoft's AI Risk Report Misses This Key Detail
items.summary: Microsoft's Digital Defense Report highlights government agencies as primary AI attack targets. It omits that many attacks exploit Microsoft software vulnerabilities.

items.title: AI-powered infostealer picks out the most profitable parts of your stolen data
items.summary: A Windows infostealer named VOLTA-AUTODOXER forwards stolen data to an AI model. The model ranks victim assets by potential revenue, guiding attackers to the most valuable information.

items.title: DarkBlinders Compromises Israeli Target and Iraqi Kurdish Government Cloud Environment
items.summary: The DarkBlinders campaign, linked to an Iran‑aligned threat actor, targeted Israel and the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. It compromised a high‑profile Israeli individual and a government cloud environment between August and October 2026.

items.title: Armadin Tests Find 88% of Severe Flaws Outside Vendor Advisories
items.summary: Armadin's testing found 88% of critical and high severity findings in client environments were not covered by vendor advisories. This indicates a gap between vendor disclosures and real-world vulnerabilities.

items.title: Nuclear threats and street brawls: Russia, Ukraine report attacks on their emergency alert apps
items.summary: After the ceasefire in Kherson lifted, Ukrainian citizens received threatening notifications on emergency alert apps. The attacks targeted the system's integrity and user trust.

items.title: Florida Student Aid Website Hack Puts Data of 4.9 Million People at Risk
items.summary: A breach of Florida's student aid website exposed personal data, including SSNs, of about 4.9 million people. The Florida Department of Education confirmed the potential exposure.

items.title: Apple warns users in 99 countries of mercenary spyware
items.summary: Apple warned users in 99 countries about mercenary spyware. The company noted the attacks' extreme sophistication and worldwide nature.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Russian and Ukrainian hackers hijack emergency apps to spread fake nuclear attack warnings
items.summary: Hackers hijacked a Ukrainian air‑raid alert system and then breached a similar Russian emergency app. They spread false nuclear attack warnings through both platforms.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Hackers disrupt refrigeration systems at European supermarkets
items.summary: Cyberattacks remotely altered refrigeration unit temperatures, disrupting supermarket chains in several European countries. The attacks caused spoilage and operational downtime.

items.title: Second wave of refrigeration cyberattacks hits European supermarkets
items.summary: A second wave of refrigeration attacks hit supermarkets in Belgium, Luxembourg, and Sweden. The attackers remotely switched temperature controls, spoiling refrigerated food.

items.title: PapRAT Cyber Espionage Campaign Leaves a 'BITTER' Taste in South Asia
items.summary:
PapRAT, linked to an India-based threat group, targeted organizations in South Asia.
The campaign used three distinct attack chains that leveraged legitimate Windows functionality.
The attacks caused significant disruption.

items.title: Bitter Deploys PapRAT in Asian Cyber-Espionage Campaign
items.summary:
Bitter deployed PapRAT across South and Southeast Asia.
The operation employed three infection chains, including one that did not use a malware executable.
The campaign aimed at espionage.

items.title: Microsoft fixes Smart App Control broken by October Windows update
items.summary:
Microsoft fixed a bug that blocked Smart App Control activation on Windows 11 after the October 2026 KB5127648 update.
The issue affected users unable to enable the security feature.
The fix is now available.

items.title: Revolve Data Breach Impacts at Least 180,000 People
items.summary:
Revolve suffered a data breach exposing personal and payment card data of at least 180,000 customers.
Hackers accessed the company's online shopping platform.
The incident was reported by SecurityWeek.

items.title: Google Introduces $250,000 Root-in-Cloud Bug Bounty Reward
items.summary:
Google announced a $250,000 bounty for discovering root-in-cloud vulnerabilities.
The reward targets high-impact findings that grant full administrative control.
The announcement was published on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Frozen part II: Hackers remotely defrost produce in Euro supermarkets ... again
items.summary:
Hackers remotely defrost produce in European supermarkets, causing significant food waste.
Multiple stores reported large puddles of melted produce at the start of the week.
The incident is a repeat of a previous attack.

items.title: Second wave of suspected cyberattacks hits supermarket freezers across Europe
items.summary:
A second wave of attacks targeted supermarket freezers across Europe, manipulating temperature controls.
The incidents caused spoilage of stock.
They followed a similar attack earlier in the month.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Trezor warns some of its wallets may hide a seed-stealing implant
items.summary:
Trezor warned that some Safe 5 wallets sold by CryptoBilis could contain a seed-stealing implant.
The implant could steal the recovery phrase from owners.
The company advises users to verify their devices.

items.title: Over 1,000 GitLab servers vulnerable to ongoing RCE attacks
items.summary:
More than 1,000 publicly exposed GitLab servers remain vulnerable to a critical remote code execution flaw.
The vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild.
The issue remains unpatched.

items.title: AI Vulnerability Finding
items.summary:
Recent analysis shows 3% of critical software bugs were discovered in the past month.
This pace could lead to an additional 100,000 bugs identified this year.
The trend highlights growing vulnerability discovery.

items.title: Critical Langflow Flaws Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code on Servers
items.summary: Two critical vulnerabilities in Langflow allow unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication or execute arbitrary code. All releases from 1.0.0 to 1.12.8 are affected, and the only fix is version 1.13.0. IBM reported the issue.

items.title: FBI pins $6.3B Binance crypto heist on North Korean hackers
items.summary: The FBI attributes a $6.3 billion Binance cryptocurrency theft to North Korean hackers. Binance is working to replace stolen funds as customers withdraw billions and the hackers continue laundering the proceeds.

items.title: Chainalysis breached using “offensive agentic techniques”
items.summary: Chainalysis suffered a data breach when external attackers used offensive agentic techniques to access its systems and internal tools. The incident is unrelated to the recent Binance hack and the specific data accessed was not disclosed.

items.title: Is Your SOC Ready for AI Agents? A Maturity Check Before You Deploy
items.summary: A 2026 survey shows 40% of security teams use AI daily and 56% are testing it, while only 4% have no plans to adopt it. SOC readiness for AI deployment requires evaluating existing capabilities before implementation.

items.title: Malicious Claude Code Extension Served in Cursor Supply Chain Attack
items.summary: A malicious Claude Code extension was delivered through a Cursor supply‑chain attack. The extension performed host reconnaissance and attempted to create a reverse SSH tunnel.

items.title: Synology warns of C3RB3R ransomware attacks targeting NAS devices
items.summary: Synology warns customers of a surge in C3RB3R ransomware attacks targeting NAS devices. The company urges immediate device updates to mitigate the threat.

items.title: Attackers Pose as IT Support on Microsoft Teams, Abuse AD CS to Steal Company Data
items.summary: Attackers impersonated IT support on Microsoft Teams, tricking employees into granting remote control. They then exploited insecure AD CS settings to obtain login certificates for privileged accounts, including a domain controller.

items.title: Could Nick Andersen’s leadership outlast the clock on his acting role?
items.summary: Nick Andersen has received praise for his leadership of CISA as acting director. With no permanent nominee yet, there is discussion of extending his acting role beyond the current deadline.

items.title: Government Linux Servers Targeted With SysGoRAT and Suspected AI-Generated Scripts
items.summary: Cybersecurity researchers identified a campaign targeting government Linux infrastructure using SysGoRAT and suspected AI‑generated scripts. The activity, observed from October 2025 to April 2026, is catalogued as CL‑UNK‑1211.

items.title: Chainalysis Discloses Data Breach Following AI-Driven Cyberattack
items.summary: Chainalysis disclosed a data breach following an AI‑driven cyberattack. Attackers used offensive agentic techniques to access the company’s systems and internal tools, mirroring the earlier breach.

items.title: FBI Attributes Binance Heist to North Korea’s TraderTraitor
items.summary: The FBI has identified North Korean APT group TraderTraitor as responsible for the largest cryptocurrency theft. The group allegedly stole over $6 billion from Binance.

items.title: FBI pins $6.3 billion Binance crypto heist on North Korea while scammers circle anxious users
items.summary: The FBI confirmed that North Korea was behind the theft of more than $6 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance. The incident occurred on or about October 29, 2026.

items.title: Ivanti patches two more Connect Secure zero-days chained in attacks
items.summary: Ivanti released security updates for two additional Connect Secure remote access gateway vulnerabilities. These flaws were part of a zero-day attack chain active since at least October 1.

items.title: Polymarket Returns $3.9 Million to Traders as DebugBear Cites DNS Hijack
items.summary: Polymarket refunded $3.9 million to traders after a DNS hijack incident involving DebugBear. The hijack was traced to compromised DNS records at the domain registrar.

items.title: Chainalysis Warns Customers After “Offensive Agentic” Security Incident
items.summary: Chainalysis disclosed an AI-driven attack that caused unauthorized activity on its platform. The incident prompted a warning to customers about potential security risks.

items.title: FBI Flags Over 600 Addresses Tied to North Korea’s Binance Heist
items.summary: The FBI identified more than 600 addresses linked to the Binance hack attributed to North Korea’s TraderTraitor. These addresses were used to launder the stolen cryptocurrency.

items.title: CyberStrikeAI in the wild: the use of AI in real-world attacks on organizations
items.summary: Researchers analyzed attacks on educational institutions that employed CyberStrikeAI for fully automated post-exploitation. The framework demonstrated AI-driven capabilities in real-world scenarios.

items.title: Ivanti Patches Two More Zero-Days Exploited in Connect Secure Attack Chain
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527 to its KEV catalog after Ivanti VPN flaws were chained in zero-day attacks. Ivanti issued patches for these vulnerabilities.

items.title: DeepSeek open-sources Super-Agent, a coding agent that watches team chats for work
items.summary: DeepSeek released a prototype coding agent that monitors team chats and can perform work on GitHub repositories. The agent operates when an allowed user requests work or a team rule permits it.

items.title: The first ten lines of a command policy for AI coding agents
items.summary: KloudStax CTO Vinay Thakker discussed setting identity, credentials, and network limits for AI agents. He emphasized that agents should run under their own identity and only act on behalf of a user when explicitly authorized.

items.title: FBI links $6.3 billion Binance crypto heist to North Korean hackers
items.summary: FBI confirms North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor behind the $6.3 billion Binance crypto theft, the largest recorded heist.

items.title: Alpine Linux rebuilds GitLab after attempted RCE attack
items.summary: Alpine Linux rebuilt its GitLab server and reset all passwords after hackers attempted a remote code execution attack on its development infrastructure.

items.title: OpenAI says it's doubling Pro usage limits and bringing Work features to Chat
items.summary: OpenAI expands ChatGPT Pro usage limits, merges usage allowances across ChatGPT and Codex, and introduces Work features directly into standard chat.

items.title: Northstar Security Exits Stealth With $7M to Expose Toxic Risk Combinations
items.summary: Northstar Security raised $7 million to exit stealth and launch a platform that maps identities, assets, and vulnerabilities, using AI agents to identify and remediate toxic risk combinations.

items.title: Week in review: Binance hit by $6.3 billion theft, impact of Brotli vulnerability
items.summary: The week’s review covers the Binance $6.3 billion theft, the impact of the Brotli compression vulnerability, and the r/opensource community’s decision to ban AI‑related projects.

items.title: CVSS 10.0 LXD, MicroCloud Flaw Lets Attackers Impersonate Trusted Clients Without a Private Key
items.summary: A critical flaw in Canonical’s LXD and MicroCloud lets attackers impersonate trusted clients by accessing the HTTPS API with a public certificate, granting them cluster and VM access without a private key.

items.title: Hackers Steal About $2.7 Million From Polymarket Traders via Hijacked DebugBear Script
items.summary: Polymarket’s site was compromised by a hijacked DebugBear script that stole traders’ positions and transferred about $2.7 million to attackers; the company is refunding affected wallets.

items.title: FBI Links North Korea's TraderTraitor to Record $6.43 Billion Binance Crypto Heist
items.summary: The FBI attributes the record $6.43 billion Binance crypto heist to the North Korea‑aligned group TraderTraitor, also known as Jade Sleet and other aliases, with support from the USSS and IRS‑CI.

items.title: NetamLoader Malware Targets Government Windows 10 Systems in Asia via .NET Injection
items.summary: Kaspersky uncovered NetamLoader, a sophisticated malware chain that targets custom Windows 10 builds used by Asian governments, deploying an undocumented .NET assembly‑loading framework.

items.title: Northflank security breach leads to abuse of customers' AI API keys
items.summary: Northflank experienced a breach that exposed customers' AI API keys. The platform is urging all users to rotate credentials and secrets stored on its service.

items.title: New Android SMS of Death exploit can remotely crash unpatched phones
items.summary: A researcher released a proof‑of‑concept for the Android CVE‑2026‑58882 “SMS of Death” exploit. It can crash unpatched phones or disrupt cellular service via a crafted text message.

items.title: Reddit to lock content behind logins to fight scrapers
items.summary: Reddit will transition to a logged‑in‑only model, restricting access to content for visitors without accounts. The change will gradually phase out public browsing.

items.title: From Beginner to Bug Hunter: Learning Cybersecurity in the AI Era.
items.summary: TryHackMe explains how AI‑generated vulnerability reports complicate bug bounty participation. It offers guidance for beginners to develop practical skills, responsibly use AI, and produce reproducible findings.

items.title: Chainalysis discloses data breach from "offensive agentic techniques"
items.summary: Chainalysis revealed a breach where attackers used offensive agentic techniques to access internal systems. The incident exposed customer names, emails, user IDs, and roles.

items.title: Chainalysis Confirms Intrusion Into Internal Tools and Exposure of Customer Identity Data
items.summary: Chainalysis confirmed an intrusion that accessed non‑sensitive customer data but did not compromise investigation content, credentials, or session tokens.

items.title: Appraisal by AI: Model-driven victim prioritization in the VOLTA infostealer
items.summary: The VOLTA infostealer deletes itself after collecting credentials, sessions, and crypto wallets. It then uses LLMs to profile victims and rank their most valuable assets.
